exclusion_detail: The abstract names no single compound; rule 2 gives analogue 6 (5'-ethyl), the most potent MraY inhibitor of the new analogues (IC50 4.5 uM) and the only one with antibacterial activity (M. abscessus). Its route from the LNA/BNA uridine 7 (which is itself 'prepared by 13 steps from D-glucose', cited, not described here) takes well over 4 reactions (three-step protecting-group sequence to 8, TFA to 9, IBX oxidation, ethynyl addition to 13, hydrogenation to 14, ribosylation, azide reduction, deprotections). All analogues 1, 4, 5, 6 are likewise long.

lead.why: Abstract names no compound; in the text 6 'showed 10- and 5-fold stronger inhibitory activity compared to 1 and 2' (IC50 4.5 uM) and is the only analogue with antibacterial activity (M. abscessus MIC50 32 ug/mL).

notes: Whichever of 1, 4, 5, 6 is taken as lead, the route is far over 4 steps and starts from a 13-step precursor 7 not prepared in this paper.
